Subject: LumenAI - procurement & marketplace path (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today - good high-level call. Quick recap and a few procurement questions so we can choose the right commercial path:

Recap:
- Use case: model serving for inference on customer data in production (real-time chat + batch embed jobs).
- Expected steady-state qps: ~120 req/s with occasional bursts; priority is predictable cost and data controls.
- Security: SOC 2 required; willing to use Dedicated or Private if needed.

Procurement / commercial questions:
1) Payment method: does LumenAI run purchases via corporate card for this size, or will you need a PO/Invoice (net 30/45)?
2) Contract paperwork: do you require a master subscription agreement + SOW, or can you accept standard Redwood terms? Is 3rd-party legal review expected?
3) Marketplace preference: are you interested in procuring via AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace, or Azure Marketplace (we can support listings on all - but the procurement path differs)?
4) Timeline: when would procurement need to be complete to start a pilot?

I've attached a short "Redwood_Marketplace_Summary.pdf" that outlines how each marketplace flow works (PO vs SaaS contract, invoicing cadence, and entitlements). Also attaching a short procurement checklist.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the procurement contact and preferred payment method (PO vs card)
- If marketplace is preferred, indicate which provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) and we can pull the marketplace AM to the thread
- If you need a paper contract, we can start a redline with our legal EAS team - usually a 2-4 week cycle depending on review scope

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps - available tomorrow 10-12 PT.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Thanks Camila - appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from our side:

1) Payment method: For initial pilot (proof-of-concept) we can use a corporate card, but for production procurement we need a PO/invoice (net 30). Preference is to do the production contract on a PO for accounting reasons.

2) Contract paperwork: We do require a master services agreement; legal will likely redline the data/indemnity sections. Expect a 4-8 week review if legal is engaged. We can prioritize an initial limited terms pilot to shorten time-to-value.

3) Marketplace preference: AWS Marketplace is preferred (we run most infra there) - having the purchase available through AWS procurement would be helpful for our finance team. GCP would be a nice-to-have, but not required for launch.

4) Timeline: Targeting pilot start in mid-December; production procurement target by end of Q1 (Mar).

I've attached our procurement questionnaire - it has our security and billing contacts. Our procurement lead (Priya Sinha) is cc'd here.

Alex
VP Product | LumenAI
alex.johnson@lumenai.com

Attachments: LumenAI_Procurement_Questionnaire.xlsx

Perfect - this is helpful, thanks Alex. A few follow-ups and proposed comms plan:

- Marketplace: we'll prioritize an AWS Marketplace pathway. That lets LumenAI procure via AWS (PO through AWS) which usually shortens internal procurement because AWS handles invoicing. I'll loop in our Marketplace PM and AWS partner contact if you want to fast-track.

- PO vs card: plan to run the pilot on card and prepare a PO-based SOW for production. I'll flag to legal that you expect MSAs + potential redlines - we can provide a minimal pilot agreement that limits scope and shortens review.

- Timeline & next steps:
  1) Camila -> Introduce our Marketplace PM + AWS partner (today)
  2) LumenAI -> Share the preferred PO template (if you have one) + point of contact in procurement (Priya, is that you?)
  3) Redwood -> Provide a draft pilot order form + statement of work for quick sign (2-3 business days)

If that looks good I'll set up a 30-minute procurement sync next week (I have Wed/Thu 9-11 PT open).
